doc.name: A — yoga catalogue, gradient backdrop, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: cork yoga mat rolled
Category: yoga
Shot programme: gradient backdrop
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing a yoga capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the tilted dynamic in a gradient backdrop treatment.

SUBJECT. A cork yoga mat rolled. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Camera rolled into a deliberate tilt with the product on a diagonal. Shoot on a 50mm anamorphic with 2x squeeze at f/2.8, framing for dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow. Stage the product on or against oiled walnut, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a neutral commercial grade with clean whites and no colour cast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
